bayts.text: The dotted Shīn, the Kāf and the Rāʾ (shukr: gratitude) (go) to the Rāʾ and the Bāʾ (Rabb: the Lord), and He is the Bāʾ and the Rāʾ (Al-Barr: the Beneficent).
Rāʾ and Bāʾ (Rabb: the Lord): to Him belongs its inverse (barr: the dry land), and to Him the Bāʾ, the undotted Ḥāʾ and the Rāʾ (baḥr: the sea).
My Ḥāʾ, my Mīm and my Dāl (ḥamdī: my praise) never cease to be His, for that in which the Bāʾ and the Rāʾ (birr: goodness) have appeared.
A Hāʾ, a Dāl and a Yāʾ (hudā: right guidance), from Him, the Yāʾ and the Sīn (Yā-Sīn: the Prophet) brought it, and he is the Ṭāʾ and the Hāʾ (Ṭā-Hā).
My Kāf and my Lām (kullī: my whole being), through him, I have given to an Alif after which (come) the Lām, the Lām and the Hāʾ (Allāh).
(I am) an ʿAyn, a Bāʾ and a Dāl (ʿabd: servant) who never ceases, through him, (to be) a Khāʾ, a Dāl and a Mīm preceded by a Yāʾ (khadīm: attendant),
of the Sīn, the Yāʾ, then the undotted Dāl (sayyid: the master, the Prophet), out of longing for a Mīm and a Wāw followed by a Tāʾ (mawt: death).
My Dāl, my Fāʾ and my ʿAyn (dafʿī: my warding off of harm), at all times, through him, is like my Jīm with a Lām followed by a Bāʾ (jalb: the drawing of good).
The dotted Ḍād and the Rāʾ (ḍarr: harm) have left me, and the Khāʾ and the Bāʾ (khabb: the deceiver) have gone back from me, laden with loss.
To my Ṣād, my Dāl and my Rāʾ (ṣadrī: my breast) there has come today the dotted Shīn, the Rāʾ and the Ḥāʾ (sharḥ: the expanding).
My Fāʾ, my Qāf and my Rāʾ (faqrī: my poverty) turns forever toward Him to Whom belong the ʿAyn, then the Zāy and the Tāʾ (ʿizza: might).
My Kāf, my Nūn and my Zāy (kanzī: my treasure) is His remembrance, and in it (are) the dotted Khāʾ, the Yāʾ and the Rāʾ (khayr: good),
together with what the inverse of “dāh” (hādin: a guide) brought, who guided: a Ḥāʾ, a Dāl and a Yāʾ, followed by a Thāʾ (ḥadīth: the Tradition),
(and it is) a Nūn, a Wāw and a Rāʾ (nūr: light) by which we are illumined, whenever a sickness, hidden within it, seizes the heart of one oppressed.
How noble is he who has attained, to the exclusion of all the nearest ones, the inverse of “barq” (qurb: nearness), and that is the Ḥāʾ and the Bāʾ (ḥubb: love)!
I have turned my face to the Lord, through the Prophet, forever: from me to Him (goes) the Qāf, then the Lām and the Bāʾ (qalb: the heart).
To Allah (goes) my Sīn and my Rāʾ (sirrī: my secret), to Him alone; and to Him — glory be to Him! — the Jīm, then the Hāʾ and the Rāʾ (jahr: the open).
My Ṣād, my Wāw and my Mīm (ṣawmī: my fasting), as long as I live, (are) for Him, and likewise the Fāʾ, then the Ṭāʾ and the Rāʾ (fiṭr: the breaking of the fast).
A Rāʾ, a Jīm and an ʿAyn followed by an Alif (rujʿā: the return) I have attained, far from all that brings an ill.
To Him (is owed) today my turning away from it, desiring that no enemies contend with me out of greed.
And He is the Wise (Al-Ḥakīm), Who has already fulfilled my wish for me, after flattery had nearly turned the matter aside.
He has fulfilled my needs in the midst of enemies, (I) an exile; and today there has come for me (the time of) composing and of teaching recitation.
There has come for me (the time of) unveiling the secrets of the Book to whoever has need of knowledge and deeds.
My return to my home has come, to make manifest what the bearers of good and of reform have come with.
Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth (Qurʾān 24:35), He alone; and no extinguishing extinguishes the Light of Allah.
And whoever wishes that what He has raised be brought low — then no concealing hides what He has made manifest.
And whoever wishes that what He hides be made open — then no disclosing makes public what He hides.
My praise, my gratitude and my contentment (go) to Him forever, through this wondrous (composition) of mine, which is black.
O you who contemplate it, go slowly with your gaze: truly the poem is black and radiant.
And pray for me and say: “O you who see my riddle: Blessed be Allah! How excellent the Bāʾ and the Rāʾ (Al-Barr: the Beneficent)!”
And in the poem there are repeated Rāʾs, yet there is in it, praise be to Allah, no repetition of the rhyme-word.
May the Bestower (Al-Wahhāb) bless and grant peace, through it, out of generosity — He has already been lavish to me, and He is the Opener (Al-Fattāḥ) and the Munificent —
upon the Bringer of glad tidings, the Warner (Muḥammad), whose servant I have become, and he is the one to whom have come elevation and exaltation.
Muḥammad, my guide in staying and in travelling: thanks to (his) company, no bereaved mother has been tried by grief.
O Lord, O He to Whom belongs its inverse (barr: the dry land), and to Him the inverse of “raḥb” (baḥr: the sea), and the dusty (earth) and the green (vault).
Give thanks for me for my gratitude and grant me success and my request, O He to Whom belong the Alif, the Mīm and the Rāʾ (amr: the Command).
And bear witness that I am well pleased with You, asking that from me toward You there endure forever the pleasing of You.
My gratitude and my whole being, in this world and the Next, (go) to the Bāʾ and the Rāʾ (Al-Barr: the Beneficent): how excellent the Rāʾ and the Bāʾ (Rabb: the Lord)!
(I), a servant to Him and an attendant, at all times, of the Ṭāʾ and the Hāʾ (Ṭā-Hā: the Prophet), and he is the Hāʾ and the Bāʾ (hiba: the gift).
May (Allah) bless him with peace; and He has kept me safe from all that contains a Ḍād followed by a Rāʾ (ḍarr: harm),
together with the Family and the Companions, until he (the Prophet) gave the noble ones glad tidings of my appearing, together with a Bāʾ followed by a Rāʾ (birr: goodness),
through him; and evils and the base have left me, every one of them; and through me a Ghayn followed by a Rāʾ (ghurr: the radiant (believers)) has triumphed.
